chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
title: Thanks to Bryant DuPre and closing of the 5 May 1983 session
summary: He credits the young historian with prompting the interview, notes life never goes in a straight line, and proposes a question-and-answer period.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: I met a young musician during these workshops that I came to know, and he always seemed to have a more than usual enthusiasm about the history of Jazz, and I must say he was more knowledgeable... Few people I know are more knowledgeable about what has happened, especially young people, in Jazz history than this young man. If he's not talking about some incident that happened, he's always asking a question about it. And at times there are things he knows and says that are enlightening to me, or would be to anybody who is three times his age. And this young man's name is Bryant DuPre, and he happens to be responsible for everything that I'm saying here, because he's talked to me about it for some time and sort of been a catalyst in getting me to do this particular thing.

I guess, to sum this up, I am sure that there's always something you forget or that doesn't come to mind. As I was talking to him the other day, I was saying that nobody's life goes in a straight line. And there are so many incidents and people that in a situation like this you don't think to mention. I'm sure after this is over, I'm going to say, 'Why didn't I say so-and-so and so-and-so?' But I think I'm going to wind this up right now.
What I'd like to do, if it's agreeable with Bryant, is have a question-and-answer period with him. He's been listening to all of this, and I'm sure there are some things

that he knows or has been reminded of that I wasn't thinking about saying, and we will probably do a lot of backtracking. But all in all, I hope I've said something that's worthwhile to some people who perhaps... Especially young people who wasn't around at certain times when certain musicians who were around. And if I've made them a little more knowledgeable about what was happening in this world of Jazz.
So right now, I think we'll close this down, and we'll have some...
